messages:
liz (sales): FYI AcmeCorp legal pushed back on our upgrade cadence for their sealed-site POC. They need guaranteed delta update windows and a clear rollback plan before signing. Can we sketch this today?
devon (solutions): Got it. Quick Q — do they want signed binaries only, or an optional agent-based delta sync?
sarah (eng-ops): Prefer signed bundles for air-gapped. Agent sync could be allowed but must be pull-only from an offline USB image or an approved repo imported by their infra team.
liz (sales): They said no outbound connections at all. USB/airdrop import only. Also asking if we can commit to monthly security patches vs quarterly feature releases.
mateo (security): For sealed networks we can do monthly security patch bundles. We'll need: SBOM, signed artifact, and CVE delta notes. Also need HSM-backed signing or vendor-signed attestations.
devon (solutions): For the POC I can propose two options:
1) Minimal POC bundle (single-node, runtime + model artifacts) delivered as a signed tarball. Upgrade cadence: safety patch only (monthly) with a manual import runbook.
2) Full POC bundle with an optional offline agent to apply deltas; cadence monthly for security, quarterly for feature rollouts.
I'll draft the runbook.
liz (sales): Pricing question: will monthly deltas change our one-off POC fee? Customer expects no extra ops cost during trial.
sarah (eng-ops): For POC we absorb one patch delivery (signing + packaging) free. Recurring monthly patching during pilot would be add-on unless they sign a support contract. We should call it out.
mateo (security): Also flag: license escalation if they require HSM-validated signatures — that's an enterprise feature with additional compliance effort.
devon (solutions): Draft runbook snippet for import flow (can be copy/pasted into their ops docs):
```
1) Place signed-bundle.tar.gz on approved media
2) Verify signature: `sha256sum signed-bundle.tar.gz && openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature signed-bundle.tar.gz.sig`
3) scp to staging host inside sealed network
4) run `./installer --apply-bundle signed-bundle.tar.gz`
5) verify services up with `systemctl status redwood-runtime`
```
liz (sales): Perfect. Can we also add a rollback command snippet? They want deterministic rollback procedures.
sarah (eng-ops): Rollback is simple for POC: stop runtime, extract previous bundle, run `./installer --apply-bundle previous-bundle.tar.gz --rollback`. Recommend tagging current live bundle as `live-YYYYMMDD` before applying.
devon (solutions): I'll include the tagging/verify checklist. Also will note max downtime estimate: 3-7 minutes for model reload on single-node POC (depends on model size).
mateo (security): From compliance side, include audit steps: audit log of imports, signature verification logs, and retention policy for old bundles.
deploy-bot: build/packager v2.14 completed: artifacts signed with key id pk-01ab. Filename: redwood-poc-20260315-signed.tar.gz
liz (sales): Thanks — can you all review the pricing blurb? I'll send to Acme tonight. Need to avoid surprise fees during trial.
sarah (eng-ops): Pricing blurb: "One-off POC packaging, signing, and on-site runbook delivery included. Ongoing monthly security patch bundles available under support agreement (recommended for sealed deployments). HSM-based signing and extended retention are enterprise options"
devon (solutions): Looks good. I'll attach the runbook and the checksum/signature verification sample to the email.
mateo (security): +1. Also offer a short screencast showing the import/verify flow — usually calms legal.
liz (sales): Awesome. I'll loop in Acme legal and ops. If they say they need guaranteed schedule window (like 2nd Tue of month), we can tentatively commit for pilot with SLA clauses. Will update here after call. :thumbsup:
